1. NEW SUBPROCESS SEAM — infrastructure/git_objects.py::GitSubprocessObjectReader.resolve_ref builds a git argv from a ref string, so it was treated as an injection surface (CWE-88/CWE-78). It is safe by construction and by measurement. Construction: _run() calls subprocess.run(args, cwd=..., capture_output=True, timeout=30) with a list argv and no shell=True anywhere in the module, so no shell metacharacter is ever interpreted; the ONE interpolated token is gated by _REF_SHAPE_RE = ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_./-]*$, whose FIRST character class excludes '-' and '.', making an option-shaped argument unrepresentable, and whose body excludes whitespace, newline, ';', '|', '&', '$', '`', '*', quotes and NUL. Measurement (20 adversarial refs driven through the real reader against this repo, read-only, no ref moved): '--upload-pack=touch /tmp/pwn', '-n', '--output=/tmp/x', '-HEAD', '--end-of-options', 'HEAD --output=/tmp/x', 'HEAD\nrefs/heads/main', 'HEAD;id', '$(id)', '`id`', '  HEAD', 'refs/heads/*', '.hidden', '' — ALL rejected by the regex before argv construction, returning None. The two shapes the regex does admit are neutralised by git itself: 'e8ddf085..HEAD' (a range) and 'a/../../etc/passwd' (traversal-shaped) both return None, because 'git rev-parse --verify' refuses a range and git's own refname rules refuse a '..' component — the '^{commit}' peel and '--verify --quiet' together admit exactly one existing commit-ish and nothing else. Both real call sites pass module constants ('HEAD', INTEGRATION_TIP_REF), so no caller-controlled string reaches this function today; the guard is second-layer defence, the same posture _SHA_SHAPE_RE already holds for first_parent. --end-of-options is NOT required here (a leading '-' cannot pass the regex) and is recorded as an INFO hardening suggestion only, for parity with the trailing '--' this module already uses in its multi-path argv.

2. WIDENED LIVENESS SET — the security question this delta really turns on is whether adding origin/develop's tip to the live-verdict sha set lets an unreviewed verdict be smuggled past a gate. It does not, because the widened rule is NOT the authorization rule. The authoritative gate is CI's security-verdict-gate, which runs features/chokepoints/verdict.py::covering_verdict — and covering_verdict is BYTE-UNCHANGED by this delta (the diff touches its name only inside the re-sorted __all__ literal). It still resolves two-hop, PR head or head's first parent ONLY, never origin/develop; it still parses the document and demands agent == 'security-reviewer', verdict == 'APPROVED' and a non-empty metrics.commit_sha; and it still fails closed on ambiguity (two qualifying candidates for one sha resolve to None). What changed is the ON-DISK HYGIENE rule (features/specs/canon.py::verdict_violations, consumed by the pre-push specs-canon scan and by SPEC-DOC-044), which matches a 40-hex FILENAME and reads no content at all — it can authorize nothing. Its input, refs/remotes/origin/develop, is local remote-tracking state that anyone with write access to the working copy could set to an arbitrary sha; that is not a new exposure, because the same actor can already bypass the entire client-side hook with 'git push --no-verify'. A pre-push hook is hygiene, never a trust boundary (DADAIA.md §3.4 chokepoint vs §3.5 'hooks validate at the publication boundary'), and the trust boundary that does matter — CI, on the server, over the PR head — was not moved by one line of this delta.

3. FAIL DIRECTION — the two consumers of the new set degrade in OPPOSITE and individually correct directions, which is the property that makes the silence in cli/commands/specs.py::_resolve_live_shas safe. The doctor degrades OPEN: when HEAD or origin/develop cannot be resolved (unfetched clone, no git context) _resolve_live_shas returns None, check_stale_verdicts returns [] and 'doctor --fix' therefore DELETES NOTHING — the fail-safe direction for a destructive auto-fix, and a direct defence against the recorded failure mode of this bug family (the tool deleting the operator's staged ship evidence). The pre-push gate degrades CLOSED: push_gate.py::_run_specs_canon_scan has no such early return; it calls live_verdict_shas directly, so an unresolvable tip merely SHRINKS the set to (head, first parent) — exactly the pre-fix strictness — and the scan keeps refusing. Silence never opens a gate; it only withholds a deletion. Read line by line, confirmed in code.

4. RULE CONSOLIDATION — 'one file per live sha' replaces 'one file total, head or parent'. The predicate is now order-independent in outcome for the doctor (discover_handoff_paths returns sorted(root.glob(...)), so duplicate reporting is deterministic) and strictly narrower per sha than the old global 'at most one': a second file naming the SAME live sha is still a violation, so a duplicate-verdict smuggle is refused exactly as before. No path that was refused for being non-live becomes accepted unless it names one of the three live shas, each of which is a sha the PR itself is built on.
